---
title: "Retrieve records for a Brazilian taxon"
format: html
---

Here we present a practical guide to `mycobank_records()` and `spfungorum_records()`, two `fungaR` functions for retrieving nomenclatural information about a Brazilian fungal taxon from [MycoBank](https://www.mycobank.org) and [Species Fungorum](https://www.speciesfungorum.org) (Index Fungorum, maintained by the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew) respectively. Unlike [`mycobank_gap()`](/articles/curate_ffb_new_records.qmd) and [`spfungorum_gap()`](/articles/curate_ffb_new_records.qmd), these are **not** comparisons against the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/) checklist — it doesn't matter whether the taxon is already registered in FFB. They are straightforward retrieval tools: give either one a species or genus, and it returns everything that repository has on record for it, filtered by default to only the names placed in Brazil.

Both functions write their results in three complementary forms: the returned `data.frame`, a downloadable `.xlsx` spreadsheet, and — by default (`html_report = TRUE`) — a self-contained **HTML report** with KPI counts and the full record table as a sortable, filterable [`DT`](https://rstudio.github.io/DT/) widget with one-click copy/CSV/Excel download buttons, opened automatically in your browser in interactive sessions (`open_report = interactive()`).

## When to use these instead of `mycobank_gap()`/`spfungorum_gap()`

- Use **`mycobank_records()`**/**`spfungorum_records()`** when you already have a taxon in mind — a single species, or every species in a genus — and want to see everything that repository knows about the Brazilian occurrence(s), regardless of FFB status.
- Use **[`mycobank_gap()`/`spfungorum_gap()`](/articles/curate_ffb_new_records.qmd)** when you want to find *candidates FFB is missing* — they add the FFB comparison step and only return names absent from the checklist.

## `mycobank_records()`: retrieve MycoBank records for a taxon

MycoBank has no public search API suited to bulk automation, so rather than scraping its live, JavaScript-driven search interface, `mycobank_records()` downloads and caches MycoBank's own bulk name export (`MBList.zip`, refreshed regularly by MycoBank, shared with `mycobank_gap()`'s cache), then filters it down to the requested species, genus, or order.

The bulk export carries no locality information, so determining Brazil evidence requires visiting each matching name's own MycoBank page (`check_locality = TRUE`, the default, via [`chromote`](https://rstudio.github.io/chromote/), a headless-Chrome driver — MycoBank's name pages are a JavaScript app with no static HTML fallback) to read the type specimen's reported "Location details", along with several other fields only available on that individual page: substrate/host, etymology, name type (e.g. Basionym/Combination), the type specimen voucher itself, its collector, and the original-publication (protolog) citation. When `require_brazil_evidence = TRUE` (the default), the result is then filtered down to only the names whose locality mentions Brazil; set it to `FALSE` to instead get every matching MycoBank name regardless of locality, with the evidence columns alongside for manual review.

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon` | Character. A single species, genus, or order name (e.g. `"Trichoderma harzianum"`, `"Trichoderma"`, or `"Xylariales"`). |
| `rank` | `"species"` (default), `"genus"`, or `"order"`. |
| `check_locality` | If `TRUE` (default), each matching name's own MycoBank page is visited to read its reported locality/substrate. Requires the `chromote` package and a local Chrome/Chromium install; skipped with a message if unavailable. |
| `require_brazil_evidence` | If `TRUE` (default), the returned table is filtered to only names whose MycoBank locality mentions Brazil. Set `FALSE` to return every matching name regardless of locality. Only meaningful when `check_locality = TRUE`. |
| `max_check` | Safety cap on how many matching names are sent through the (one-page-load-per-name) locality check. Default `200`. |
| `mycobank_dir` | Local directory used to cache the downloaded MycoBank export (~140MB). Defaults to `"mycobank_download"`. |
| `save` | If `TRUE` (default), saves the result as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet. |
| `html_report` | If `TRUE` (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above. |

### Value

A data frame, one row per matching MycoBank name and, by default, with a Brazilian MycoBank locality, with its MycoBank number, author, year, name status, classification, current name, full synonymy text, **original MycoBank URL** (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), and — when `check_locality = TRUE` — several fields scraped from the name's own MycoBank page: `MycoBank_Locality`, `MycoBank_Substrate`, `MycoBank_Etymology`, `MycoBank_Name_Type`, `MycoBank_Type_Specimen`, `MycoBank_Collector`, `MycoBank_Protolog`, and a `MycoBank_Brazil_Evidence` flag.

### Example

```r
library(fungaR)

# All MycoBank information for a single species, only if MycoBank places it in Brazil
sp <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma harzianum")

# Every MycoBank species-level name in genus Trichoderma with a Brazilian MycoBank locality
genus_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus")

# Every matching name regardless of locality, for manual review
all_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                                require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)

# Faster, without the per-candidate locality check (no Brazil filtering possible)
fast_records <- mycobank_records(taxon = "Trichoderma", rank = "genus",
                                 check_locality = FALSE)
```

## `spfungorum_records()`: retrieve Index Fungorum records for a taxon

Species Fungorum/Index Fungorum has no bulk export, but it does publish a public, documented web service (`fungus.asmx`, a plain HTTP GET/XML API - no SOAP client, headless browser, or authentication required) that `spfungorum_records()` queries directly. A single request returns every name matching `taxon`, including, for many records, the type specimen's own reported `LOCATION` and `HOST` - no per-record page visit needed, unlike MycoBank.

Index Fungorum's `LOCATION` field very often names a Brazilian state directly (e.g. `"Pernambuco"`) rather than the country itself, so `Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence` checks the location against the country name and every Brazilian state name (with or without diacritics), not just the literal word "Brazil".

### Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `taxon` | Character. A single species or genus name (e.g. `"Phellinotus neoaridus"` or `"Phellinotus"`). |
| `rank` | `"species"` (default) or `"genus"`. Index Fungorum's web service has no operation for searching by higher classification, so order-level searches are not supported. |
| `require_brazil_evidence` | If `TRUE` (default), the returned table is filtered to only names whose Index Fungorum location mentions Brazil. Set `FALSE` to return every matching name regardless of locality. |
| `max_number` | Maximum number of matching names requested from the web service in a single call. Default `1000`, generous for any genus. |
| `save` | If `TRUE` (default), saves the result as an `.xlsx` spreadsheet. |
| `html_report` | If `TRUE` (default), also writes the interactive HTML report described above. |

### Value

A data frame, one row per matching Index Fungorum name and, by default, with a Brazilian reported locality, with its Fungorum number, author, year, name status, current name, **original Species Fungorum URL** (rendered as a clickable link in the HTML report), `Fungorum_Location`, `Fungorum_Host`, and a `Fungorum_Brazil_Evidence` flag.

### Example

```r
library(fungaR)

# All Index Fungorum information for a single species, only if it reports a
# Brazilian locality
sp <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus neoaridus")

# Every Index Fungorum species-level name in genus Phellinotus with a
# Brazilian reported locality
genus_records <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus", rank = "genus")

# Every matching name regardless of locality, for manual review
all_records <- spfungorum_records(taxon = "Phellinotus", rank = "genus",
                                  require_brazil_evidence = FALSE)
```

## Additional Tips

- Install the [`chromote`](https://rstudio.github.io/chromote/) package (and have a local Chrome/Chromium install) to include `mycobank_records()`'s locality check; without it, that step (and the Brazil-evidence filtering that depends on it) is skipped with a message, and every matching name is returned unfiltered. `spfungorum_records()` needs no such extra dependency - locality (when available) always comes back with the same request.
- `mycobank_dir` is shared between `mycobank_records()` and `mycobank_gap()` - pointing both functions at the same directory avoids re-downloading MycoBank's bulk export twice.
- For larger genera, `mycobank_records()`'s per-candidate locality check can take a while - start with `check_locality = FALSE` to size up how many names match before running the full Brazil-evidence check. `spfungorum_records()` has no equivalent slow step: it is always a single request regardless of genus size.
